title: Normalized DVR tower carried by a normalized derived coefficient sequence
statement: For l,E,W,D and l different from D.p as in [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower], every normalized derived coefficient sequence N of [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site] admits a normalized DVR tower T whose finite objects are isomorphic to the actual derived evaluations of N. Its specified total limit coefficientSequenceLimit(N) has a Roos triangle [def-weil-derived-limit] whose projection to level n, after the evaluation isomorphism, is exactly coefficientSequenceProjection(N,n). In particular the tower and maps are constructed from the given sequence, without asserting any finite-effectivity conclusion.

source.place: Integral coefficient clause: interpreting compatible finite reductions as a completed-coefficient tower and identifying its derived inverse-limit projections; Stacks Tags 0940 and 0941.

proof.text: Take T.M(n) to be the actual derived evaluation of N, T.tau to be the localized coefficientSequenceTransition, and T.tower to be the derived exact scalar restriction of N. On ordinary section maps prove identity, composition and compatibility with completed-coefficient restriction: all are the presheaf identity and composition equations, with the canonical restriction-of-scalars associators. This includes equal indices and hence every identity transition.

For arbitrary exact functors, verify that their localized transition maps and induced comparison isomorphisms satisfy the same equations: use localization extensionality, the factorization isomorphisms on complexes, and cancellation. Apply these generic proofs to the ordinary equations. The resulting derived equations supply tau_refl, tau_comp and tower_tau. Use the supplied normalization of N for the normalization field of T. The finite comparison isomorphisms e(n) can therefore be identities.

Apply the canonical Roos triangle of the restricted tower. By the definition of coefficientSequenceProjection its n-th projection is the completed-tower projection followed by the finite evaluation isomorphism. Composing with the inverse of that isomorphism cancels it. Product extensionality identifies the first arrow with the precise product lift in the statement.

lean.statement:
theorem coefficientSequence_roosModel
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E] (W : Scheme.{t})
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{d}) (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (N : coefficientSequenceDerived l E W) (hN : IsNormalizedCoefficientSequence l E W N) :
    ∃ (T : NormalizedDVRTower l E W D hl)
      (e : ∀ n : ℕ, T.M n ≅ (coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation l E W n).obj N)
      (hp : HasProduct (fun n : ℕ ↦
        (normalizedDVRTowerEvaluation l E W D hl n).obj T.tower)), letI := hp
      ∃ δ, IsDerivedLimitTriangle
        (fun n : ℕ ↦ (normalizedDVRTowerTransition l E W D hl n.le_succ).app T.tower)
        ((coefficientSequenceLimit l E W).obj N)
        (Pi.lift (fun n : ℕ ↦ (coefficientSequenceProjection l E W n).app N ≫
          (normalizedDVRResCompleted l E W D hl n).map (e n).inv ≫
          (T.evaluationIso n).inv)) δ
